title: Smallest String Starting From Leaf
spaceBreakdown:
- string path: up to h characters → O(h)
- string rev (temporary per leaf): up to h characters → O(h), freed after each leaf
- recursion call stack: up to h frames → O(h)
- not counted: string best (returned output), input tree
approach: Every valid string corresponds to a root-to-leaf path reversed. We perform a DFS from the root, maintaining the current path as a string. At each leaf, we reverse the path to obtain the leaf-to-root string and keep the lexicographically smallest one seen. Standard C++ string comparison (`<`) correctly handles the prefix rule (shorter prefix is smaller), so no special length logic is needed.
hints: Each leaf of the tree defines exactly one candidate string - what in the tree determines the characters and the order of that string?

Use depth-first search with backtracking: maintain the current root-to-leaf path, and at each leaf reverse it to get the leaf-to-root string. In Example 1, reaching leaf 3 (under node 1) gives path "abd", reversed to "dba" - the current best.

```
dfs(node, path):
    if node is null: return
    append node's char to path
    if node is a leaf:
        candidate = reverse(path)
        if best is empty or candidate < best:
            best = candidate
    else:
        dfs(node.left, path)
        dfs(node.right, path)
    remove last char from path
```

**Root with only right child** - root has one child, must not be treated as a leaf.
`Input: [0,null,1]` → `Expected: "ba"`
⚠️ Bug: checking `if (!node->left)` for leaf detection → root has no left child, treated as leaf → returns "a"

**Longer string is lexicographically smaller** - a deeper leaf can produce a smaller string.
`Input: [1,0,0,0]` → `Expected: "aab"`
⚠️ Bug: preferring shorter strings with `if (rev.size() < best.size())` → "ab" (len 2) preferred over "aab" (len 3) → returns "ab"

**Prefix tie** - one candidate is a prefix of another; the shorter must win.
`Input: [2,2,1,null,1,0,null,0]` → `Expected: "abc"`
⚠️ Bug: comparing character-by-character without checking length when one string ends → "abc" and "abcc" compare equal through 3 chars, keeps first found "abcc" → returns "abcc"

followUps.q: What if each node can have any number of children (n-ary tree) instead of just two?
followUps.a: The DFS with backtracking approach generalizes directly - iterate over all children instead of just left and right. The path string and reversal logic stay identical. TC: O(n·h), SC: O(h), unchanged.

followUps.q: Return the k-th lexicographically smallest string instead of the smallest.
followUps.a: Maintain a max-heap of size k. At each leaf, push the reversed string; if the heap exceeds size k, pop the largest. The top of the heap at the end is the k-th smallest. TC: O(n·h·log k), SC: O(h + k).

followUps.q: Count the number of distinct leaf-to-root strings.
followUps.a: Insert each reversed string into a hash set at each leaf, then return the set size. TC: O(n·h), SC: O(n·h) in the worst case when all strings are distinct.
